(Correction: titles, not games) So I searched all Steam titles, sorted them by user reviews, checked first 3 pages and sorted out the titled released in 2015. And the titles are from least upvoted to most upvoted:

Fran Bow

A creepy point and click adventure game that tells the story of Fran, a young girl struggling with a mental disorder and an unfair destiny.

Contradiction - Spot The Liar

A full-motion video murder mystery adventure!

Doom & Destiny

No, it's not a crossover of Doom and Density. Instead, it is a JRPG made with Game Maker and is full of parodies and references.

Higurashi: When They Cry Hou - Ch.1 Onikakushi

A visual novel with strong characters. Unlike many visual novels where content is cut to fit Steam rules, this game is something that is for the whole family from the start.

Hyperdimension Semicolon Neptunia Re;Birth3 V ;; Generation

JRPG with animÃ© girls. It is based on gaming consoles and gaming industry. Has some fanservice.

Postal 2: Paradise Lost

A DLC for Postal 2. Does not include a Portal gun.

Secrets of Grindea

Warning: Early access. A cheery action RPG. Has a co-op mode with up to 4 players being able to play together. For additional value, there's also a fleshed out, challenging roguelike mode to truly put your ARPG skills to the test!

TIS-100

A very nerdy open-ended problem solving game. You have to create commands that turn input values to the desired ones and then output them from designated locations. Zachtronics fans know what's up.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 - Scandinavia

DLC for Euro Truck Simulator 2. Now you can drive around in Scandinavia.

Hook

Nothing Peter Pan related here. Instead it's a minimalistic puzzle game where you have to disentangle puzzles.

Layers of Fear

"A psychedelic horror where you take control over an insane painter in his quest to finish his magnum opus. Heavily inspired by the masterpiece paintings from the past centuries, and the architecture and dÃ©cor from the XIX century."

Nuclear Throne

Now out of early access. Author's connections aside, it's a well-done action rogue-lite game. Takes place in post-human post-apocalyptic nuclear wasteland. Has a great game feel.

Broforce

Very 'murican game with great game feel. You control parodies of action heroes from the 80s, 90s and other eras. Is as complex as it's explosive.

Undertale

This is a JRPG heavily inspired by Mother series. This has two main themes: your choices matter and you not having to kill a single thing. Great characters and humor.

Kerbal Space Program

Little green men want to explore their star system so spacecraft need to be made to launch into air. Unlike Spore, this is actually not so casual and greatly benefits from that. Trying to overcome physics provides a good challenge.

Assault Android Cactus

An intense arcade-style twin stick shooter. Has local co-op. Hard to describe.

Infinifactory

Imagine TIS-100 and Spacechem but in 3D! Get inputs to point A to B and in most missions you have to alter them in the way. Being a problem solving game, the solutions are up to you. Even the most trivial to solve puzzles can be incredibly challenging to optimize.

Downwell

A simple roguelite platformer where you have to descend an incredibly deep well. Great game feel.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Hearts of Stone

DLC for The Witcher 3. More of an expansion pack. "In an age where $10 DLC will get you a skin and a half or access to nebulous, pre-order locked content, Hearts of Stone is an offering even more generous than the free DLC and improvements that CDPR has already showered upon the initial release of Wild Hunt."

Eternal Senia

An action RPG. One of the best parts of it is that it's free!

Crypt of the Necrodancer

One of the best and easiest-to-search titles aside, imagine a rythm and roguelike game combined! Coupled with great soundtrack and you can boogie&fight your way through the levels. Note that the game is rather challenging.

Kung Fury

Somehow a film got into this list. Contains Hitler!

Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes

An asymmetric co-op. There's a bomb. One person has to disarm it and others have to help to defuse it. Only a defuser can see a bomb but others can see the manual.

So how many of them have you heard about? Which ones have you played?
[Recommendation] So I sorted Steam titles by "User reviews" and am going to list the games (and other titles) that were released in 2015 and are on first 3 pages. 23 games remained on the list.

I played Undertale for the first time last night.

It blew my mind; it's really a game meant for people who love games (if that makes sense)- it completely subverts your expectations of RPGs- it's one of the coolest things to come out of 2015 and I can't believe I took so long to play it (I have a big backlog).

I also played Assault Android Cactus and really enjoyed it, it wound up on my list of favorite top-down shooters.

I heard about a lot of those, but haven't played a single one. Incidentally, I'm not interested in a single game on that list.

That said, there is something interesting about that list, and namely that Steam user reviews alone are probably not the be-all and end-all in determining what makes a "good" or interesting game. It is interesting that, aside from a piece of Witcher 3 DLC, the list doesn't include any meaningful AAA titles, or heck, any "big" or "popular" titles at all, for that matter. What is happening here, I suspect, is that the people interested in playing these titles rate them very high, and the titles are probably very good for people who are interested in those respective kinds of games to begin with, but most of those also seem like incredibly niche games.

For example, based on the user ratings, "Higurashi: When They Cry Hou - Ch.1 Onikakushi" is probably an incredibly good "visual novel", and "Hyperdimension Semicolon Neptunia Re;Birth3 V ;; Generation" is probably really good if you're into "JRPGs with animé girls.", but the truth is, very few people (in the grand scheme of things) are.

I think that 2015 had some incredible game releases, but none of them to be found in the first three pages of top-rated Steam reviews, instead it's a list of mostly obscure niche titles and indie games. Now there's absolutely nothing wrong with those, but it just seems like that list is heavily biased by people self-selecting to review the kinds of obscure niche games they themselves will likely find interesting to begin with, rather than a more generally representative list of what "most" Steam customers will find to be good games (because the more popular, bigger games are under a lot more scrutiny and therefore will inherently produce more mixed reviews, as a much broader audience of people will review and rate them, not just the group that will like these games to begin with anyway).
So basically, games that are not for everyone but are great for what they are!

Hey, Doom & Destiny is there. I enjoyed the hell out of that game when it was on XBLIG. Highly recommended.

Edit: and Keep Talking is also there. Great party game, wish I had a VR headset for it though.
